todo_line: - [ ] 001 Record the architecture decision before further implementation.
outcome: Record an accepted ADR that fixes the concrete first-class group-membership and Messaging subscription architecture required by iteration 064 before any executable implementation proceeds.
scope: Create the next sequential record, `docs/adr/0025-use-first-class-group-memberships-and-member-owned-conversation-subscriptions.md`, and add its accepted entry to `docs/adr/README.md`.

Name the Membership consistency boundary, aggregate/stream identity, commands, immutable events, and fields that distinguish enduring club membership from a fresh `group_membership_id` for every genuine custom-group admission and exact removal.

Define caller-generated identity for new admissions and a deterministic, retry-safe identity/append-only reconciliation contract for each provable active legacy relation; state how legacy `GroupMemberAdded` and `GroupMemberRemoved` facts replay without inventing unproved periods.

State explicitly how Everyone/Admin system-group consequences remain compatible and whether first-class group-membership identity applies to them, while preserving ADR 0024 club membership, role, and Admin-continuity ownership.

Name the Messaging member-owned subscription aggregate/stream, canonical follow/subscription facts, server-resolved authorization provenance, idempotent group-membership revocation contract, and durable completion receipt.
Specify order-independent behavior for delayed old follows, ordinary unfollow, alternate authorizing group memberships, remove/re-add/new follow, handler retry, and aggregate restart.

Define how manual follow and successful root/reply auto-follow use one authoritative operation without trusting product-supplied provenance, and how historic `MessageSent`/follow shapes are reconciled once without legacy scans in the live path.
Clarify that projection barriers coordinate read-model visibility only, while removal completion relies on the Messaging domain receipt and current authority is rechecked through provider handoff.
scope_exclusions: Do not change application code, migrations, tests, feature files, acceptance tags, designs, iteration plan/todo files, or behavior in this packet.
Do not implement the group-membership projection/reconciliation, removal use case, subscription ledger, revocation handler, UI, or acceptance scenarios.
Do not reopen stakeholder-approved business choices such as keeping empty groups, preserving full history on re-add, clearing old follows, or preserving club roles.
Do not preserve the existing conversation-by-conversation cleanup fan-out or infer correctness from projection cutoffs/generations.

references.facts: Implementation Plan step 1 requires the ADR before implementation; steps 2-6 and Open Technical Decisions constrain the identities, ownership, reconciliation, member-owned stream, revocation receipt, provenance, and barrier contracts the ADR must make concrete.
ADR index currently ends at 0024; add one concise accepted row for ADR 0025.
Use the repository Date, Status, Context, Decision, and Consequences structure; recent ADRs also link relevant reference guidance and state supersession where applicable.
Membership and Messaging are separate Commanded contexts; Messaging depends on Membership through a public contract and must not mutate Membership state or query its aggregates/storage directly.
Caller-generated typed UUID identity remains accepted, although ADR 0024 superseded its club-membership routing/preflight choices; the new ADR must describe its relationship to this identity rule.

A projection barrier proves selected read models reached a checkpoint but does not prove later asynchronous domain work completed; iteration 064 requires an explicit Messaging receipt for that completion.

Club owns active club membership and role/Admin invariants, explicitly does not claim an unbounded arbitrary-group matrix, and leaves future arbitrary group-membership consistency to a boundary chosen around its own invariants.
Choose aggregate boundaries around immediate invariants and express cross-aggregate/context workflows through explicit domain contracts.
Keep command ownership explicit and do not use query projections as the write-side authority.

Historical events remain immutable; deterministic projection derivations and new domain facts require different reconciliation strategies, and production-history compatibility must be replayable and retry-safe.
Assign authorization, lifecycle, subscription, and coordination responsibilities to explicit collaborators with public contracts.

`Memba.Membership.Club` currently stores `group_memberships` by `{group_id, club_membership_id}` and applies `GroupMemberAdded`/`GroupMemberRemoved` by toggling one reusable active relation; `AddCustomGroupMember` authorization also currently executes at this boundary.
The current read model overloads `membership_id` as club membership and stores an `active` flag rather than a distinct group-membership identity.
The current strong Membership handler scans projected group conversations and dispatches one Messaging unfollow per conversation; this fan-out is the rejected correctness mechanism.
The current aggregate is conversation-owned, records only person IDs, and derives sender auto-follow directly from `MessageSent`; it has no authorizing group-membership provenance.
The current projection independently derives root/reply follow state from `MessageSent`; the approved architecture makes canonical subscription facts the replay source instead.
Existing provider handoff already has a current-access recheck boundary that the ADR should preserve while changing subscription authorization.

constraints: Set the ADR status to `accepted`: the approved plan says there are no open business or technical decisions and requires this record to bind subsequent implementation.
Use unambiguous field language such as `club_membership_id` and `group_membership_id`; do not silently reuse the existing ambiguous `membership_id` for both concepts.
Choose and name the custom-group lifecycle consistency boundary and its concurrency guarantee; do not leave Club-versus-Group ownership as an implementation-time decision.
Give concrete command/event/receipt and aggregate/stream names sufficient for later packets to implement one coherent model; keep incidental module layout flexible where it is not architectural.
Preserve Membership as current group-participation authority and Messaging as subscription/delivery authority, with cross-context communication through public idempotent contracts.
A re-add must create a new group membership; ended membership authorization stays ended. Revoking one authorization must not erase another current group membership's authorization.
Product/UI/message callers may request follow behavior but may not assert trusted group-membership provenance; the authoritative operation resolves it from Membership.
Reconciliation must be deterministic, restartable, append-only where new aggregate facts are required, and conservative where source history cannot prove a lifecycle period.
Keep legacy source events replayable and identify any ADRs this record amends or partially supersedes rather than rewriting their historical text.
This is documentation-only, so project rules do not call for `dev check`.

Report successful `git diff --check` and link-resolution evidence with exit statuses.
